html:
Sheikh Hasina was prime minister of Bangladesh from 1996 to 2001 and again from 2009 to 2024, longer than anyone else. Her rule ended when she fled the country during a popular uprising.

She was born in 1947, the eldest child of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, the founder of Bangladesh. On 15 August 1975 army officers killed her father, her mother and her three brothers, the youngest aged ten. She and her sister were abroad and lived. She spent six years in exile in Delhi.

She came home in 1981 to lead her father's party, the Awami League. With her rival Khaleda Zia, the widow of another murdered leader, she helped bring down military rule in 1990. The two women then took turns in power and their feud ruled politics for thirty years.

After 2009 the economy grew by 6 per cent or more a year. The clothing industry boomed (see Rana Plaza), poverty fell and the Padma Bridge was built. She took in the Rohingya refugees in 2017.

She also jailed opponents and won three elections that were boycotted or widely called unfair. Critics disappeared. In July 2024 students rose against her, and on 5 August she left for India by helicopter (see the July uprising).
sum: Sheikh Hasina was prime minister of Bangladesh from 1996 to 2001 and again from 2009 to 2024, longer than anyone else. Her rule ended when she fled the country during a popular uprising.
